description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:106-117

```rust
fn tls_alg_to_x509_oid(hash_alg: u8, sig_alg: u8) -> Option<ObjectIdentifier>
```

The set of (hash_alg, sig_alg) pairs `pkix-ct` will accept is
hardcoded in this private function. A caller wanting to know,
before they fetch an SCT, "is the algorithm pair (h, s) supported?"
has only three options:

1. Read the rustdoc table in the module-level comment (which is
   informational, not authoritative — the implementation could
   diverge).
2. Construct a synthetic SCT with the algorithm pair, call
   `verify_*`, and inspect for `Error::UnsupportedSignatureAlgorithm`.
3. Pin to a specific pkix-ct version that they've reviewed.

This information ought to be a contract clause. Either:

- Make `tls_alg_to_x509_oid` `pub fn` (rename to
  `pub fn supported_signature_oid` to emphasize it's a public
  interface), OR
- Expose a `pub const SUPPORTED_TLS_ALGORITHMS: &[(u8, u8)] =
  &[(4, 3), (5, 3), (4, 1), (5, 1), (6, 1)];`, OR
- Expose an iterator `pub fn supported_algorithms() ->
  impl Iterator<Item = (u8, u8)>`.

This matters for:

- Caller setup code that wants to declare its capabilities to a CT
  log monitor (e.g. an upstream component asks "which algorithms
  can your verifier handle? we'll filter our SCT stream").
- Conformance test tooling that wants to exercise every supported
  algorithm.

Priority P3 because the workaround (trust the rustdoc) works for
careful callers, but a programmatic check is what a downstream
library author would want.

Also: `pkix-path::SignatureVerifier` exposes a similar contract; if
`pkix-ct` exposes its own table, the two need to remain in sync.
PKIX-ppbr.12 (algorithm dispatch via pkix-path) is the structural
fix for this — once both crates share a single source of truth, the
table here vanishes. So priority P3 also because PKIX-ppbr.12 is
the better long-term answer.
title: tls_alg_to_x509_oid is private — caller cannot enumerate supported (hash_alg, sig_alg) without trial-and-error
